orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Explain the availability of water on Earth
orchestrator_output.text_narration:
Our Earth is often called the 'Blue Planet' because it looks mostly blue from space. This blue colour comes from the huge amount of water present on its surface.

But how much of this water is actually available? About 71% of the Earth's surface is covered by water. This means almost three-fourths of our planet is water!

Most of this water, about 97%, is saltwater found in oceans and seas. This water is too salty for us to drink or use for farming. Only a small part, about 3%, is freshwater.

Now, let's look at this small 3% freshwater. Most of it is locked up in ice caps and glaciers, especially at the North and South Poles. A good amount is also found underground as groundwater. Only a very tiny fraction is available as surface water in rivers, lakes, and ponds.

So, even though Earth has a lot of water, only a very small portion is freshwater that we can easily use for drinking, cooking, and other daily needs. This is why it's so important to save water!
